bull.b: Achieving complete amino-acid detection strengthens the technical foundation of Proteus and advances the company toward a broader, more capable sequencing workflow. Incorporating this capability into the developmental kit could improve product usefulness and support commercialization in 2027.

The reported throughput and accuracy advantages indicate meaningful potential product differentiation within protein sequencing. If these development results translate into commercial instruments and customer workflows, they could support adoption, improve research productivity, and strengthen Quantum-Si's market position.

A substantial cash position and runway into late 2028 give Quantum-Si time to execute Proteus launch activities without immediate financing pressure. Lower operating-expense and cash-use guidance also indicate improved cost discipline while the company completes commercialization work.

bear.b: The sharp revenue decline shows that current commercial demand remains weak during the transition to Proteus. A very small and shrinking revenue base limits operating leverage, reduces evidence of recurring customer adoption, and leaves the business dependent on successful future launch execution.

Heavy recurring cash burn and large operating losses indicate that the current business model is not yet self-funding. Continued deficits can erode the capital base and may eventually require additional financing if Proteus revenue does not scale sufficiently after launch.

bear.t: Supply Chain And Launch Execution Risk
bear.b: Longer component lead times create execution complexity ahead of the Proteus launch and require earlier purchasing commitments. The resulting inventory and working-capital needs could increase near-term cash demands, while delays or shortages could affect production readiness and customer delivery.
